findings.finding: _is_cache_guarded assumed the old uv run "<guard>" shape (tokens[:3]); every SessionStart command now tokenizes as uv run --no-project "<guard>" ..., so test_forward_registered_as_one_consolidated_session_start_command failed for all 12 hook-bearing plugins.
The integration test claimed to derive its command from the real shipped hooks.json entry, but discarded the resolved path and ran a hand-written argv, only asserting prefix equality.

The fixture's regex only matched an already-pinned uv run --no-project "..." command, so a future regression (flag dropped) would raise a misleading 'fixture broken' error instead of a flag-missing assertion.
_collect_command_strings is duplicated from test_hooks_uv_run_pinned.py instead of shared/imported.
Six hook scripts' module docstrings still showed the old unpinned uv run "..." invocation example, contradicting the now-mandatory writing-plugin.md convention.

The mini-plan wrongly said plugins/shipwright-iterate/hooks-codex/hooks.json needed editing ('remaining lines get the flag'); that file's only 2 commands were already fully pinned pre-diff. This stale sentence caused both external code-review passes (glm + openai) to independently raise a false HIGH 'file missing from diff' finding.

Claim under doubt: Hook scripts are stdlib-only apart from pyyaml in audit_compliance_on_stop.py, so --no-project changes nothing about how they behave (spec probe #5). — The audit in probe #5 only looked at each hook script's own top-level imports. It did not follow code that runs in a child process. That child process now runs without pyyaml. Concrete failing chain: plugins/shipwright-iterate/hooks/hooks.json SessionStart runs `uv run --no-project run_if_cache_ready.py ... check_required_checks_hook.py ...`. run_if_cache_ready.py:110 starts each target with `[sys.executable, target]`. check_required_checks_hook.py:162 starts the producer with `[sys.executable, tools/check_required_checks.py, ...]`. check_required_checks.py:220 calls `all_workflow_check_names()`, which imports `lib.automerge_readiness` inside the function (shared/scripts/lib/required_checks_drift.py:48). That module does a plain `import yaml` at line 30. Before this change, a session in the Shipwright repo (root pyproject.toml declares pyyaml, jsonschema and openai) made `uv run` sync the root project, so sys.executable was the project venv and had yaml. Now the interpreter is a bare one and the import raises ModuleNotFoundError. The producer exits 1, which is not in `_EXPECTED_EXITS = (0, 2)`. The hook then prints `producer exited 1, which it does not document` once per throttle window, never records a success, and the required-checks drift check stops working in the repo that uses it most. No test catches this. The meta-test only reads hooks.json, and the integration test only runs write_terminal_marker.py, which has no dependencies.
findings.suggestion: Any one of these. (a) Add `--with pyyaml` to the SessionStart run_if_cache_ready command. It must be added in ALL plugins, not only iterate: codex_hook_inventory keys run_if_cache_ready by the same relative path everywhere, so a different prefix in one plugin raises BundleCollisionError. (b) Have the producer or the hook treat ImportError as a documented exit 2 or a skip. (c) Repeat the dependency audit through the whole child-process and import chain, not just top-level imports, and show that no hook-reachable path imports yaml, jsonschema or openai. Then correct the spec's 'exactly one third-party dependency' claim.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: `uv run --no-project --with pyyaml audit_compliance_on_stop.py` behaves the same as before (probe #5 checked only that it exits 0). — audit_compliance_on_stop.py runs the full A-I compliance audit in the same process. Group D's manifest loader (plugins/shipwright-compliance/scripts/audit/_group_d_manifest.py:39) imports jsonschema inside a function and fails closed, returning None, when it is missing. In the Shipwright repo, jsonschema used to come from the synced root project. Now only pyyaml is available, so `traceability_findings` (_group_d_traceability.py:275-279) quietly downgrades D-orphan and D-layer from evaluated to SKIP 'manifest ... schema-invalid'. The hook still exits 0, so the probe #5 check passes while local diagnostics lose coverage. The on-stop docstring's claim that the audit chain is 'first-party + stdlib' is already wrong for this path.
findings.suggestion: Add `--with jsonschema` to both audit_compliance_on_stop callers with an identical prefix (the prefix-consistency test enforces that). Or accept the D-layer SKIP deliberately and record it as a known residual next to the .venv/.python-version one.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: After this change, hook execution never tries to find, resolve or sync the project in the session's working directory. — One hook script starts its own `uv run` child without the flag. plugins/shipwright-build/scripts/hooks/cleanup-review-scratch-on-code-reviewer-failure.py:232 runs `subprocess.run(["uv", "run", str(script), "cleanup", ...], cwd=str(resolve_project_root()))`. That working directory is the user's project, which is exactly the directory this iterate is about. If it is an unrelated uv-managed project, that SubagentStop path still syncs it (the os error 32 exposure). It then runs review_scratch.py under that project's interpreter. The hook fails open, so the scratch diff is quietly left behind. The meta-test cannot see this because it only reads hooks.json. The same unpinned pattern exists outside hooks in shared/scripts/lib/held_merge_reconciliation.py:214/234. Several SKILL.md and reference files also tell the agent to run `uv run "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/..."` from the target project's directory (for example plugins/shipwright-adopt/skills/adopt/SKILL.md:64+ and plugins/*/skills/*/references/step-0-*.md). They have the same failure mode, but the agent runs them, not the hooks.
findings.suggestion: Insert `--no-project` into that argv; test_cleanup_review_scratch_on_code_reviewer_failure.py:94 only checks args[:2], so it stays green. Either extend the scope statement to name the skill-instruction and non-hook call sites as a known follow-up, or explain why they are unaffected.

findings.finding: Claim under doubt: The static meta-test fails whenever any hooks.json `uv run` command is missing --no-project. — `_UV_RUN_PREFIX = r'uv run((?:(?!uv run)[^"])*)"'` only matches when a double quote follows the flags. A command like `uv run "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/x.py"` is caught. `uv run scripts/x.py` or `bash -c 'uv run x.py'` (no double quote) produces no match, so it adds no offender and the test passes. The external openai code review raised this (medium). code_review_reply.json has no disposition for it; only the hooks-codex false positive was dispositioned.
findings.suggestion: Also assert that every command containing the token sequence `uv run` produces at least one prefix match (or tokenise with shlex), so an unquoted or single-quoted command becomes an offender instead of being skipped. Or record a reasoned decline, for example by pointing to test_hooks_json_quoting.py already forcing quoted placeholders.

findings.finding: AC-1 and the mini-plan both explicitly require `plugins/shipwright-iterate/hooks-codex/hooks.json` to be edited ("2 lines already correct, remaining lines get the flag"), and `_MIN_EXPECTED_FILES = 13` in the new meta-test counts it. The diff contains no change to that file. If its remaining `uv run` entries are unpinned, AC-1 is unmet and `test_every_uv_run_hook_command_has_no_project` will fail against `shipwright-iterate/hooks-codex` on the very next CI run — the change is self-inconsistent with its own new guard.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same `--no-project` insertion to every remaining `uv run` entry in `hooks-codex/hooks.json` (and re-run the meta-test).

findings.finding: The test's premise — "derives its command from the actual shipped hooks.json entry" — is only cosmetic. `_find_real_uv_run_command` locates the real entry, but the subprocess is then launched with a hardcoded `["uv", "run", "--no-project", str(script_path)]` and a separately reconstructed script path (`REPO_ROOT / "shared" / "scripts" / "hooks" / _TARGET_SCRIPT_NAME`). The fixture's `prefix` is only used for an equality assert, and the raw hooks.json path is discarded, so if hooks.json pointed the entry at a different script (or a plugin-local copy), the test would still run its own reconstruction and pass. The docstring overstates what's proven.
findings.suggestion: Either build the subprocess argv from the fixture's `prefix` and the path resolved from the hooks.json entry (substituting `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`), or soften the docstring; the current form would pass against a hooks.json entry that doesn't actually exist in the shipped shape.

findings.finding: Missing return type annotation for a function returning a `tuple` (docstring says "Pull the exact … command", implying a string) — and more substantively, the regex `r'(uv run --no-project)\s+"([^"]' + re.escape(script_name) + r')"'` only ever matches commands that already carry `--no-project`, so the fixture cannot detect a regression back to unpinned form in a useful error message; it raises a confusing "fixture broken" assertion instead of "the flag was removed". Minor, but the failure mode is misleading.
findings.suggestion: Match `uv run(?: --no-project)?` and assert on the presence of the flag separately, so a real regression surfaces as such.

findings.finding: The flag-skipping loop `while parts[0].startswith("--")` assumes all pre-script flags are bare (valueless) tokens. If a future `uv run --project foo "script"` or any flag-with-value were added before the script, the value token (`foo`) would be misread as the script path. Not broken for the current `--no-project`-only shape, but the guard is narrower than the comment implies.
findings.suggestion: Acceptable as-is for today; if touched again, parse up to the first quoted token rather than filtering on `--` prefixes.

findings.finding: The operator resync instructions themselves invoke `uv run shared/scripts/tools/build_codex_plugin.py …` and `uv run shared/scripts/tools/codex_hooks_sync.py …` without `--no-project` — the very pattern this iterate establishes as the repo convention and which `test_hooks_uv_run_pinned.py`/`writing-plugin.md` now mandate for hooks. These are docs, not hooks.json, so the meta-test doesn't catch them, but an operator following the doc from an unrelated uv-managed CWD would hit the exact bug this PR fixes while applying the fix.
findings.suggestion: Add `--no-project` to those two documented commands.
